attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post, responding to a fan's AGI prediction he describes.

semantics.note: 'It wasn't' answers the fan's AGI prediction just before it. The proposition, that Grok 3 as demoed was not AGI, is a fair reading and is stated as fact, not hedged.

contract.note: The plain reading of AGI as broad, roughly human-level general competence is ordinary and fair. The result turns on that reading and on independent broad evaluation of the launch version.

evidence.note: Karpathy's short launch-day 'vibe check' found mixed successes and failures. He says it was informal, and it is not a broad human-level evaluation, so it does not meet the contract's measurement requirements.

reviews.rationale: The only item is Karpathy's informal test, which shows uneven ability but no systematic, broad assessment of the launch checkpoint against a human-level standard. Company material was excluded as the rules require. Marcus's own Update 2 paraphrase cannot prove his claim. The packet does not settle the support or contradiction condition.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The present perfect 'has clearly failed' is read as a historical observation up to publication. The proposition keeps 'clearly' and the 'pure pretraining' scope.

contract.note: Reading the claim as failure so far, with AGI meaning broad human-level intelligence, is an ordinary and fair plain reading. It does not stretch the claim into a prediction that pretraining can never produce AGI.

evidence.note: This January 2025 scientific synthesis records uneven capabilities, failures on simple reasoning, and weakness with novel scenarios. That means broad human-level intelligence had not been shown by publication.
OpenAI's GPT-4 report separates pretraining from post-training. It frames the scope but says nothing about AGI either way.
ARC Prize (December 2024) judges that o3 is not AGI and that simple scaling is not enough. o3 uses test-time compute, so it does not test pure pretraining directly.
The 'Sparks' paper calls GPT-4 an early, incomplete AGI. That is a qualified claim and does not meet the broad human-level standard, but it does test the word 'clearly'.

reviews.rationale: The support condition is met. A contemporary synthesis (e1) documents material gaps in general-purpose systems before publication, and the independent ARC Prize view (e3) agrees that even systems beyond pure pretraining were not AGI. The strongest counterevidence, Sparks (e4), calls GPT-4 incomplete and does not meet the contradiction condition.
